newsitem.title: USA: Germany's Herzog bought by Xebes Galleon.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Herzog bought by Xebes Galleon.

text.p: Herzog GmbH, a privately-held German manufacturer of men's leather and sportswear, said on Tuesday it had been acquired by Xebes Galleon Inc, a publicly-traded U.S. shell corporation.
Herzog shareholders would become controlling shareholders of the publicly traded entity, it said, and the company's name would be changed to Herzog International Holdings Inc.
The company, which would continue to trade under the symbol until the symbol was formally changed in mid-November, said it was completing a four million mark private placement of stock in Germany.

Proceeds would be used to restructure debt, secure more licenses, and purchase new computer equipment, it said. Select Capital Advisors arranged and negotiated the terms of the merger and would oversee the private placement through its offices in Germany and internationally.

Since 1994, Herzog has had a licensing agreement to manufacture goods for Yves Saint Laurent. It said it planned to obtain similar agreements from other fashion leaders, as part of efforts to double sales and profitability in the next five years.

Herzog said it anticipated revenues of 10 million marks for fiscal 1996, and of 15 million marks for fiscal 1997, which ends Oct. 31, 1997. The company said it expected to report earnings of 1.5 million marks for fiscal 1996.
